column1: # TIER-2 HELD-OUT CASES, SET 2. Created 2026-10-27, one row.
# WHY A SECOND HELD-OUT FILE. docs/validation-cases.tsv is the development set,
# frozen 2026-10-23, and at least seven config.yaml settings were accepted or
# rejected against its rows. docs/validation-cases-heldout.tsv was read on
# 2026-10-26 and is therefore spent: a held-out set is spent the first time it is
# read, which is the whole point of one. So on 2026-10-27 the project held NO
# unread evaluation data, and that -- not a shortage of ideas -- is why the 5/11
# figure cannot be improved on by any amount of tuning.
# THE ONE RULE: no threshold decision may consult this file until the thresholds
# are final. Not "should not". If a config.yaml value is changed because of a row
# in here, this file becomes a second development set and the project is back
# where it started on 2026-10-26.
# Score with (and only when the set is worth spending):
#   python scripts/retrospective.py --cases docs/validation-cases-heldout-2.tsv
# DISCLOSED: it was scored once on 2026-10-27, immediately after the row was
# written, to check the row parses and the assay id resolves. The result was
# `watch` / agrees. Nothing in config.yaml was changed because of it and nothing
# may be; one bit is out, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying so.
# DISCLOSED AGAIN, 2026-10-28: scored a second time after the Quackenbush row was
# proposed, for the same reason -- to check it parses -- and the whole file was read,
# because --cases scores every row. So all three rows are now out, and they say:
#   Cryptosporidium_18SrDNA_Xiao_1999_round2    works  -> watch         agrees
#   MONKEYPOX_dsDNA_G2R_generic_TaqMan_Li_2010  works  -> declining     DISAGREES
#   Pan_HERPES_dsDNA_Polymerase_round2          works  -> low coverage  weaker
# ONE FALSE ALARM IN THREE HELD-OUT ROWS, and it is the informative one: Mills 2022
# validated the G2R generic assay on 2022 outbreak clinical specimens, and the shipped
# config calls it `declining`. The development set's false-alarm rate is 4/32 = 12%;
# this is 1/3, on three rows, so the interval is useless (95% CrI 4%-82%) and the
# POINT of recording it is that the number exists and was not chosen. Nothing in
# config.yaml was changed because of it, and under the file's own rule nothing may be.
# The honest status of this file is now: partially spent, 3 bits out, and worth no
# further reads until it holds enough rows to be worth spending.
# Same columns and same bar as the development set: a paper, erratum or redesign
# reporting how an assay ALREADY IN THE REGISTRY performed, with `as_of` no later
# than the sequences its authors could have seen. A new assay's validation
# against its own panel does not qualify -- it says nothing about drift.
# Target: 15-20 cases, at least 5 with `mechanism: drift`. Both earlier sets are
# dominated by coverage-type failures, so the drift flag still rests on about one
# ground-truth event; that is the gap to close first.
# Leads: scripts/check_candidate_identity.py over
# docs/2026-10-26-retrospective-candidates.tsv is now the cheapest source, because
# it answers the question that actually blocks a row -- did the citing paper test
# OUR oligos -- before any reading time is spent. See ROADMAP.md, tier-2 validation.
assay_id
# ROW ADDED 2026-10-27. The first CONFIRMED retrospective identity in the project:
# both round-2 primers are printed verbatim in the paper and read `exact` against
# the registry (docs/journal/2026-10-27-leetz-identity-confirmed.md). `as_of` is the
# received date, 25 March 2007, not the publication date.
# `works`, and the mechanism matters. The paper's headline is 73.8% positive for
# the Xiao nested 18S primers, which against detect_fraction_threshold: 0.90 looks
# like a miss -- but Table 2's denominator is an oocyst DILUTION SERIES on one
# isolate (>10^4 down to 10^0), so the misses are at low template. That is
# sensitivity, which this tool does not model: a primer that matches perfectly
# still fails at one oocyst. On the isolate itself the assay worked twice -- the
# round-2 product digested cleanly with Vsp I to 628 + 104 bp, and the procedure
# was repeated with a German bovine stock "with identical results". Recording it
# as `fails` would teach the harness that a sensitivity result is a coverage
# result, which is exactly what the `mechanism` column exists to prevent.
Cryptosporidium_18SrDNA_Xiao_1999_round2
column5: 10.1007/s00436-007-0567-y Leetz 2007 Parasitol Res 101:951-962: round-2 primers printed verbatim (Xiao18SF2 GGAAGGGTTGTATTTATTAGATAAAG, Xiao18SR2 AAGGAGTAAGGAACAACCTCCA) and amplified C. parvum HNJ-1 genotype II, RFLP-typed cleanly with Vsp I (628 + 104 bp), repeated on an independent German bovine stock with identical results; the 73.8% in Table 2 is a dilution series, i.e. sensitivity, not coverage

column1: # ROW ADDED 2026-10-27. Mills, Greninger et al. 2022 (J Clin Virol 159:105373, PMC9783225, open access)
# prints the G2R generic primers and probe character for character -- identical to
# MONKEYPOX_dsDNA_G2R_generic_TaqMan_Li_2010 -- and validates them on 2022 outbreak clinical
# specimens across many sample types (20 MPXV-positive swabs in the quantitative comparison).
# `works`, mechanism blank: a clinical validation of the stored oligos on circulating virus.
# `as_of` is the paper's received date, 2 November 2022. Identity was read directly from the
# open full text, not inferred from the citation.
MONKEYPOX_dsDNA_G2R_generic_TaqMan_Li_2010
column5: 10.1016/j.jcv.2022.105373 Mills 2022 J Clin Virol 159:105373: G2R forward GGAAAATGTAAAGACAACGAATACAG, reverse GCTATCACATAATCTGGAAGCGTA, probe AAGCCGTAATCTATGTTGTCTATCGTGTCC printed verbatim and validated on 2022 clinical specimens; G2R outperformed F3L by ~0.4 Ct

column1: # NOT A ROW, recorded so the lead is not chased twice:
# Cryptosporidium_18SrDNA_Xiao_1999_round1 reads VARIANT against the same paper --
# the round-1 pair Leetz tested is not the one the registry holds, however much it
# cites Xiao 1999. ENTEROVIRUS_ssRNA_VP3_VP1 (+round2) and
# INFLUENZA_A_ssRNA_Matrix_gene_recognized_h_2003 are closed as UNCONFIRMABLE by
# CONTENT rather than by access: Ng 2025 reprints its own CDC2022 redesign and
# cites the Nix gold standard only, and Slomka 2023 prints no primer table at all.
# ROW PROPOSED 2026-10-28, AWAITING MAINTAINER SIGN-OFF. Quackenbush et al. 1998
# (Virology 246:392-399, received 26 February 1998) USES the VanDevanter pan-herpes
# DPOL nest this entry holds -- it cites VanDevanter 1996 by name and all four oligos
# (DFA, KG1, TGV, IYG) occur verbatim in its text -- and reports what it found: a
# ~250 bp round-2 band from five green turtle fibropapillomas, whose sequence is only
# 53% identical to its nearest relatives (BHV-1, PRV) across the 183 bp between TGV
# and IYG. That is the pan-family claim doing exactly what it is for: amplifying a
# herpesvirus roughly half-divergent from anything then known, now Chelonid
# herpesvirus 5. `works`, mechanism blank.
# WHY IT IS PROPOSED RATHER THAN WRITTEN BY ME: the works/fails call is the
# maintainer's. Strike the row if you read it differently -- the arguable part is that
# the paper also reports tumour-free skin and two olive ridley turtles as PCR
# NEGATIVE, which is a true negative for those samples and not an assay failure.
Pan_HERPES_dsDNA_Polymerase_round2
column5: 10.1006/viro.1998.9207 Quackenbush 1998 Virology 246:392-399: cites VanDevanter 1996 and prints DFA/KG1/TGV/IYG; ~250 bp round-2 product sequenced from five green turtle fibropapillomas, 53% identical to BHV-1/PRV between TGV and IYG (PROPOSED, awaiting sign-off)

column1: # NOT A ROW, recorded 2026-10-28 so the lead is not chased twice:
# 10.1016/j.mimet.2008.12.003 reads CONFIRMED against Salmonella_invA_Rahn_1992 -- the
# first new CONFIRMED since 2026-10-27 -- and is still not a case. It is Suess, Flekna,
# Wagner & Hein 2009 (J Microbiol Methods 76:316-319; the retrospective queue and the
# fetch list both called it "Malorny"), a METHODOLOGICAL study: a synthetic 100 bp
# template flanked by Rahn's primers 139/141, then eight forward primers and six probes
# carrying deliberate mismatches, each measured for quantification error. Our oligos are
# printed because they are the scaffold of someone else's experiment, and nothing in it
# reports the Rahn assay performing on anything real. Its finding -- primer-region
# mismatches cost up to 63% in quantification while barely changing the curve, probe-region
# mismatches up to 33% and worse in kind -- is recorded as a C2 prior source in
# docs/bayesian-scoring-plan.md instead.
